$$
{\begin{aligned}5x+2y=7 \\ 3x-4y=8.\end{aligned}
$$

 
According to Cramer's rule, the unknown $x$ can be written as 
$x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}|}$, where ${D}_{x}=$
questions.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x+2y=7 \\ 3x-4y=8.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is 

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{x}$, we replace the first column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}7 & 2 \\ 8 & -4\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving for a Coefficient in a 2x2 Linear System Using Cramer's Rule
questions.problem:
Let $⟨x,1⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x-y=k \\ x+4y=3\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

- $|\begin{aligned}3 & k \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|=5$
- $|\begin{aligned}3 & k \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|=-7$
- $|\begin{aligned}3 & k \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|=13$
questions.worked_solution:
The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =12+1 \\  & =13.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $y$ is given by $y=\frac{{D}_{y}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}3 & k \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D} \\ 1 & =\frac{|\begin{aligned}3 & k \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|}{13} \\ |\begin{aligned}3 & k \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}| & =13\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "III only".

questions.problem:
Let $⟨-1,y⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+ky=-4 \\ 3x-4y=5.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

- $|\begin{aligned}2 & k \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}|=-2|\begin{aligned}-4 & k \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}|$
- $|\begin{aligned}2 & k \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}|=|\begin{aligned}-4 & k \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}|$
- $|\begin{aligned}2 & k \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}|=-|\begin{aligned}-4 & k \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}|$
questions.worked_solution:
The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}2 & k \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $x$ is given by $x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}-4 & k \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D} \\ -1 & =\frac{|\begin{aligned}-4 & k \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}2 & k \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}|} \\ |\begin{aligned}2 & k \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}| & =-|\begin{aligned}-4 & k \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "III only".

$$
{\begin{aligned}9x+11y=-14 \\ 6x-ky=-34.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

- $|\begin{aligned}-14 & 11 \\ -34 & -k\end{aligned}|=-4|\begin{aligned}9 & 11 \\ 6 & -k\end{aligned}|$
- $|\begin{aligned}-14 & 1 \\ -34 & -k\end{aligned}|=4|\begin{aligned}9 & 11 \\ 6 & -k\end{aligned}|$
- $-4|\begin{aligned}-14 & 11 \\ -34 & -k\end{aligned}|=|\begin{aligned}9 & 11 \\ 6 & -k\end{aligned}|$
questions.worked_solution:
The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}9 & 11 \\ 6 & -k\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $x$ is given by $x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}-14 & 11 \\ -34 & -k\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D} \\ -4 & =\frac{|\begin{aligned}-14 & 11 \\ -34 & -k\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}9 & 11 \\ 6 & -k\end{aligned}|} \\ -4|\begin{aligned}9 & 11 \\ 6 & -k\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}-14 & 11 \\ -34 & -k\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "I only".

questions.problem:
Let $⟨x,3⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}kx+3y=1 \\ 7x-2y=8.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

- $-3|\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}|=|\begin{aligned}k & 1 \\ 7 & 8\end{aligned}|$
- $3|\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}|=|\begin{aligned}k & 1 \\ 7 & 8\end{aligned}|$
- $|\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}|=3|\begin{aligned}k & 1 \\ 7 & 8\end{aligned}|$
questions.worked_solution:
The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $y$ is given by $y=\frac{{D}_{y}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}k & 1 \\ 7 & 8\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D} \\ 3 & =\frac{|\begin{aligned}k & 1 \\ 7 & 8\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}|} \\ 3|\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}k & 1 \\ 7 & 8\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "II only".

questions.problem:
Let $⟨x,-2⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}15x+8y=-1 \\ kx+13y=-31.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

- $|\begin{aligned}15 & 8 \\ k & 13\end{aligned}|=2|\begin{aligned}15 & -1 \\ k & -31\end{aligned}|$
- $|\begin{aligned}15 & 8 \\ k & 13\end{aligned}|=-4|\begin{aligned}15 & -1 \\ k & -31\end{aligned}|$
- $-2|\begin{aligned}15 & 8 \\ k & 13\end{aligned}|=|\begin{aligned}15 & -1 \\ k & -31\end{aligned}|$
questions.worked_solution:
The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}15 & 8 \\ k & 13\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $y$ is given by $y=\frac{{D}_{y}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}15 & -1 \\ k & -31\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D} \\ -2 & =\frac{|\begin{aligned}15 & -1 \\ k & -31\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}15 & 8 \\ k & 13\end{aligned}|} \\ -2|\begin{aligned}15 & 8 \\ k & 13\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}15 & -1 \\ k & -31\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "III only".
